Preserve lossless submission during normal operation: capacity exhaustion must not silently discard work or cause the caller to mark unprocessed work complete.
Preserve stable group-to-queue routing, FIFO processing, and one worker per queue.
Keep offset registration before an accepted item can be processed, and retain compatibility with existing queue statistics and shutdown behavior.
items.notes: A positive finite queue maxsize with blocking put() is sufficient; no particular capacity is required. A depth check alone is insufficient if concurrent submissions can bypass the bound. Raising queue.Full is not a safe substitute here: the existing strategy catches submission exceptions and marks the message offset complete. This finding concerns queued backlog, not a guarantee that all memory usage is bounded.

items.defectStatement: The query key in useTraceItemAttributeKeys identifies cached attribute keys only by queryOptions, omitting the organization used by the fetcher. Requests for different organizations with identical options can therefore share a cache entry and reuse another organization's TagCollection.
obligations: Distinguish cache entries by the current organization used by the attribute-key fetcher, even when queryOptions are identical.
Ensure an organization change updates the effective query key; memoization must not retain the previous organization's key.
Preserve queryOptions as part of cache identity so existing distinctions between project, datetime, and attribute/dataset options remain intact.
items.notes: An organization slug or another stable, unambiguous organization identifier is valid. The shown scope has no organization binding or useOrganization import, so adding organization.slug alone in the cited lines would not compile; a valid replacement must obtain the identifier through available, valid code. Cache isolation does not by itself guarantee that usePrevious cannot temporarily display prior data while fetching; changing that separate behavior is not required by this finding.

items.defectStatement: The redirect traversal in add-buffer.lua was reduced from an inclusive 0–10000 loop to 0–1000, so longer redirect chains can stop at an intermediate span rather than the terminal set. Subsequent redirect writes and set merges then use that intermediate ID, potentially splitting a segment across buffers.
obligations: Restore at least the previous traversal allowance (inclusive iterations 0 through 10000), or otherwise correctly resolve chains supported by that allowance independently of the 1000-span eviction cap.
Preserve traversal from parent_span_id and termination when a redirect is missing or points to the current set_span_id.
Preserve redirect_depth reporting for existing terminating chains and leave set_span_id holding the resolved target for downstream writes and merges.
Keep traversal bounded or otherwise ensure cyclic redirects cannot cause the script to run indefinitely; preserve the separate 1000-span retention behavior.
items.notes: Lua numeric for-loop bounds are inclusive: the current loop performs up to 1001 lookups, not exactly 1000. A chain just over 1000 links does not necessarily select the wrong target; failure occurs when the loop exhausts before reaching it. Restoring 10000 is sufficient and does not promise correctness for arbitrarily deep chains.

items.defectStatement: Both ZUNIONSTORE calls use Redis's default SUM aggregation, so a member present in both input sorted sets receives the sum of its scores instead of retaining a timestamp score. This artificially raises duplicate members' eviction priority and causes the later ZPOPMIN trimming to retain them ahead of genuinely newer spans.
obligations: Prevent duplicate-member scores from being added in both the span-key merge and the parent-key merge; retain an input timestamp score for each duplicate.
Preserve the union of distinct members and the scores of members present in only one input.
Preserve the existing merge conditions, source cleanup after merging, and accurate span_count tracking so the subsequent size-limit trimming still works.
items.notes: MAX or MIN aggregation are both acceptable; equal timestamp scores must remain unchanged. 'Effectively never evicted' is overstated: eviction is rank-based, and inflated scores delay eviction rather than make it impossible. No unrelated aliasing or redirect behavior change is required for this finding.

items.defectStatement: The overflow eviction at lines 62–64 removes the lowest-scored members without protecting the segment span whose span_id equals set_span_id. If that span is present among the eviction candidates, trimming can leave the buffered segment without its segment/root span.
obligations: Preserve any existing segment-span member whose span_id equals set_span_id when trimming an overflowing set, regardless of its score.
Reduce an overflowing set to at most 1000 members, counting the protected segment span toward that limit and evicting the lowest-scored eligible non-segment members.
When no segment-span member is present, retain the existing lowest-score eviction behavior; leave sets of 1000 or fewer members unchanged.
Preserve retained members' payloads and scores, the set's expiration, and the surrounding script's return and root-presence behavior.
items.notes: Only lines 62–64 are replaceable. The shown script merges existing sorted sets; it does not insert an incoming payload here. Protection must identify the actual member by span_id, not assume the current span_id or is_root_span identifies the segment member. Removing victims and restoring the segment is valid only if the final size still respects the cap and its original score is preserved. The remote-span and downstream-flush details are not demonstrated in this window.

items.defectStatement: Making the header’s .contents a flex container can prevent a long, non-wrapping topic title from shrinking: the header-extra-info component’s outer flex item retains its automatic minimum width, which is not removed by overflow:hidden on an inner wrapper. The title can consequently push the navigation panel outside the header rather than truncate with its existing ellipsis.
obligations: Allow the flex item containing header-extra-info to shrink below its title’s intrinsic width when header space is constrained.
Preserve the title’s existing truncation and ellipsis behavior while keeping navigation visible within the header when the available width accommodates the non-title controls.
Preserve the header’s flex layout, vertical centering, and existing navigation ordering and alignment.
items.notes: The supplied window does not show the component markup or inner overflow rule, so the wrapper relationship is contextual information from the finding. A scoped rule added within the cited replacement can address the actual flex item; applying min-width:0 only to an inner non-flex wrapper is insufficient. Equivalent sizing or overflow solutions are valid if they preserve truncation and do not merely clip the navigation.

items.defectStatement: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb, the method at lines 153–155 is named include_website_name rather than the serializer inclusion hook include_website_name?, so its presence check does not control serialization. Because website_name is also absent from untrusted_attributes, it can expose the website’s host and sometimes path even when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) hides website.
obligations: Ensure the serializer actually applies an inclusion condition to website_name.
Omit website_name whenever scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) is true, even if the website is present.
Omit website_name when website is blank; for unrestricted users with a present website, preserve inclusion and the existing website_name computation.
Preserve the existing restrictions and serialization behavior of other user fields.
items.notes: The replacement is limited to lines 153–155; adding website_name to the earlier untrusted_attributes declaration is outside that edit range. Renaming the hook alone does not close the disclosure. The shown code establishes serialization exposure, but does not itself establish how clients display the value.

items.defectStatement: In remove_member, deleting the membership through group.users.delete(user_id) does not explicitly clear the removed user's primary_group_id when it points to this group. This can leave a user referencing a group they no longer belong to as their primary group.
obligations: Continue removing the specified user's membership in the specified non-automatic group.
Persistently clear the specified user's primary_group_id if it equals the group being removed.
Preserve primary-group assignments pointing to other groups and do not modify other users' primary-group assignments.
Preserve the automatic-group rejection and existing save/JSON response flow; a nonexistent user ID should remain harmless.
items.notes: The historical destroy_deletions behavior and exact flair/title consequences are not established by the supplied code. A conditional database update or an equivalent removal operation with the required cleanup is valid; the finding's suggested implementation is not mandatory.

items.defectStatement: The added call loads fallback locales only when ApplicationController#set_locale runs; it does not itself cover translations in background jobs or mailers that bypass this controller. If fallback locales are not otherwise loaded lazily, those translations can miss entries that exist in fallback locale files.
obligations: Ensure fallback translations are available in non-request translation paths without requiring a prior web request.
Preserve fallback translation availability for web requests and the existing selection of the user's effective locale or the site default.
Preserve fallback precedence and locale scoping, including restoration of the previous locale after I18n.with_locale.
items.notes: The window establishes only the controller-local loading call, not the claimed absence of loading elsewhere. The cited single line cannot ordinarily fix non-request paths: a complete fix would generally require changes to shared locale-loading behavior or non-request callers outside this replacement scope. Removing this call alone is not a fix unless equivalent loading is already guaranteed elsewhere.

items.defectStatement: TopicEmbed.import_remote fetches url with open(url).read before any local URL or destination validation, allowing unsafe destinations or redirects to be contacted if an attacker-controlled URL reaches it. The HTTP(S) check in import runs only after the fetch and therefore cannot protect this request from SSRF.
obligations: Validate the initial URL before any fetch: accept only HTTP(S) URLs and permitted web ports, and reject malformed or non-network inputs without opening them.

Prevent connections to private, loopback, link-local, or otherwise non-public destinations, including IPv4 and IPv6 addresses obtained through DNS; validation must apply to the destination actually contacted.
Disable automatic redirects or subject every redirect destination to the same scheme, port, and destination restrictions before contacting it.
Preserve successful fetching of permitted public articles and pass their response body to Readability with the existing tags and attributes, retaining the existing title override and import behavior.
items.notes: The controller/job path and host validation described in the finding are not shown, so their exact behavior cannot be confirmed here. A nonstandard port on an allowed public hostname does not by itself target an arbitrary internal host, and ignoring the path is not inherently an SSRF flaw. A timeout alone does not prevent SSRF; a hardened fetch helper is valid only if its protections actually enforce the destination restrictions.

items.defectStatement: The body extraction in PollFeed#poll_feed unconditionally calls scrub on i.content, which can be nil for RSS items whose body is supplied only through description. Such an item raises NoMethodError and interrupts processing of the feed instead of importing its description or skipping it if it has no body.
obligations: Use the item's description as a fallback when content is nil, while preserving preference for available content.
Skip items with no usable body without raising or calling TopicEmbed.import for them, and continue processing subsequent items.
Preserve encoding scrubbing and HTML entity unescaping for the selected body before import.
Preserve the existing import arguments and URL selection behavior for items that have a body.
items.notes: Only line 35 is replaceable, so any fallback and per-item skip must fit there without relying on changes to surrounding lines. A nil-based fallback followed by a blank-body check is valid; falling back for blank content as well is also acceptable. The synchronous TopicRetriever caller is not shown, but the exception would propagate to any unprotected caller.

items.defectStatement: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, TopicUser.find_by can return nil for the current user and topic, but the code immediately reads tu.notification_level. With no TopicUser record, unsubscribing raises NoMethodError instead of persisting a notification preference and showing the topic.
obligations: Handle an absent TopicUser record by obtaining or initializing a usable record for the current user and requested topic, with a valid notification level for the comparison.
Preserve the existing transition for existing records: levels above regular become regular; levels at or below regular become muted.
Ensure the missing-record path also persists the resulting notification preference through the subsequent save! and reaches the existing response handling.
items.notes: Only lines 105–107 are replaceable; later assignments and tu.save! still require a non-nil, saveable tu. A nil guard on the comparison alone is insufficient. TopicUser.get is valid only if its actual contract supplies the required record and notification level; initializing or creating a record is also valid. The email scenario is plausible but not established by the shown code.

items.defectStatement: The category-selection queries access row 0 without checking for an empty result. A missing embed_category setting, an embed category with no matching category, or a missing uncategorized_category_id fallback can therefore abort the migration before hosts are migrated.
obligations: Handle an empty embed-category query result without accessing a nonexistent row, and proceed to the uncategorized-category fallback.
Preserve selection of the matching embed category when its ID is nonzero, including integer conversion of the returned ID.
Preserve use of the uncategorized_category_id setting when the primary category resolves to zero or is absent; handle an empty fallback result without an exception.
Ensure category_id has a deterministic integer default when neither query supplies a usable value, so the unchanged host-insertion code can continue.
items.notes: The exact exception is adapter-dependent: some result objects raise on an out-of-range row index rather than returning nil and causing NoMethodError. Guarding only a nil result object does not handle an empty result set. The shown code does not establish a required default category ID; do not require a particular numeric default or changes outside the cited lines.

items.defectStatement: The public group-members route calls model.findMembers() only once without requesting additional pages. With the reported default limit of 50 and no pagination controls in the public view, non-automatic groups with more than 50 members expose only the first page rather than the full membership previously available.
obligations: Make members beyond the default first page accessible on the public group-members view, including groups spanning multiple pages.
Use pagination or all-members behavior actually supported by the member-loading API; do not assume an arbitrary large limit guarantees complete results.
Preserve the group controller's showing='members' state and the members controller's group model binding.
Keep empty groups and groups fitting within one page working, and ensure any additional page loads retain earlier members rather than replacing them.
items.notes: The shown code establishes the single call, but not the API's default limit or historical behavior; those details come from the finding. Only lines 8–12 may be replaced, so adding hypothetical controls elsewhere is not a sufficient fix. Full retrieval or pagination wired to an actually reachable public-view mechanism can both be valid.

items.defectStatement: The downsizing loop writes to the path of an already-open Tempfile without refreshing its file handle. If downsizing replaces that path with a new inode, the loop's tempfile.size checks and the subsequent Upload.create_for call can use the original file's size and contents rather than the reduced image.
obligations: After a successful downsizing operation, subsequent size checks must reflect the current reduced image, including when the output replaces the input inode.
Leave tempfile referring to the current image with its contents readable from the beginning, so the unchanged Upload.create_for call receives the reduced contents and matching size.

Preserve the existing eligibility checks and bounded behavior: only nonempty images with a positive size limit are candidates, and perform at most five 80% downsizing attempts, stopping when the current size is within the limit.
Preserve the animation setting passed to downsizing and maintain compatible temporary-file cleanup through the existing ensure block.
items.notes: The inode-replacement behavior is conditional; the shown code does not establish how OptimizedImage.downsize writes its output. Refreshing/reopening the handle or using a separate output tempfile are valid approaches. Merely changing the loop to File.size(tempfile.path), or rewinding the old descriptor, is insufficient because the unchanged downstream call still uses tempfile and tempfile.size. Do not require that five attempts always bring every image under the limit.

items.defectStatement: In get_committable_offsets, the numeric range scan stops at an absent offset even when later tracked offsets are complete, unnecessarily limiting the committable offset across legitimate Kafka offset gaps. The finding overstates permanent blockage: after mark_committed removes the completed prefix, the existing min_offset logic can skip the gap on a subsequent call.
obligations: Return the highest completed tracked offset before the first outstanding tracked offset, without treating untracked numeric gaps as blockers.
Never advance past an outstanding tracked offset above last_committed, including when later offsets complete first.
Only return tracked offsets strictly greater than last_committed; omit partitions with no newly committable offset and preserve independent per-partition results.
Preserve the existing locking and mark_committed lifecycle: querying must not discard pending commit candidates or mark them committed before the caller successfully commits.
items.notes: Only lines 86–96 are replaceable. Scanning existing tracked offsets in numeric order is valid; a new submission-order deque is not required and would need changes outside this span. For example, completed offsets 10 and 12 should yield 12 immediately; if 12 is outstanding, yield 10. Preserve the current returned-offset convention, without adding 1.

items.defectStatement: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits StatefulDetectorHandler but leaves its required abstract members unimplemented, so constructing the handler for MetricAlertFire raises TypeError instead of returning a usable handler. The previous handler was an instantiable placeholder whose evaluate method returned an empty list.
obligations: Make MetricAlertDetectorHandler concrete and instantiable through the existing detector-handler construction path.
Preserve compatibility with QuerySubscriptionUpdate packets and the handler interface expected by detector callers.
Preserve the placeholder behavior of evaluating packets without producing detector evaluation results; do not introduce unsupported metric-alert issue generation.
items.notes: A concrete-base approach or suitable implementations of the abstract members can be valid; stateful metric-alert functionality is not required. Merely suppressing abstractness is insufficient if evaluation then fails or emits spurious results. Only the cited class lines are replaceable, so any newly needed names must be available or introduced within that replacement.

items.defectStatement: In tableResultComponent, the feature-enabled branch supplies TableWidgetVisualization with no columns, no rows, and empty metadata instead of the current result and query configuration. Consequently, table widgets rendered through this branch cannot display returned table data.
obligations: Supply the feature-enabled visualization with the current result's rows and metadata, retaining available field types and units rather than replacing them with empty objects.
Supply columns derived from the corresponding query at index i, preserving configured field order and the existing derived-metric prefix normalization.
Keep each visualization paired with its own result and query, and handle absent query fields without introducing a crash.
Preserve the feature gate and the existing feature-disabled rendering path, including its loading and span-widget behavior.
items.notes: Changes are limited to the cited branch. Use the actual TableWidgetVisualization prop contract; adapting result metadata to that contract is valid, and defaults for genuinely absent metadata are acceptable. The finding does not establish that all legacy renderer options must be replicated in the new visualization.

items.defectStatement: OrderedQueueWorker.run unconditionally completes the current offset in its finally block, even when processing raises an exception or queue.ShutDown. This removes failed work from the outstanding set and can allow commits to advance past an unsuccessfully processed message.
obligations: Complete the current work item's partition and offset only when its processing succeeds; leave failed processing outstanding so commits cannot advance through that offset.
Continue completing successfully processed items, including successful items handled after an earlier failure, without clearing the earlier failed offset.
Preserve exception logging and continued worker operation for ordinary processing exceptions, and preserve termination on queue.ShutDown without completing the interrupted item.
Preserve queue-depth metric emission on both successful and exceptional processing paths.
items.notes: The shown commit loop passes offsets directly to commit_function; it does not itself add one, so the finding's offset+1 claim is not established here. Leaving an offset outstanding prevents unsafe commits but does not itself retry or immediately redeliver the failed item. Replacement is limited to lines 144–149; any restructuring must keep the following metric call valid and preserve its execution on failure.

items.defectStatement: The helper recognizes only strings equal to `count()` after case folding and outer whitespace removal. Consequently, equivalent count expressions accepted by the query language, such as an explicitly aliased count or supported internal whitespace variants, are left unweighted instead of being converted to `upsampled_count()`.
obligations: Recognize supported syntactic variants of a standalone zero-argument count aggregate, including explicit aliases and whitespace variants, and convert them to the weighted aggregate.
Preserve an explicit output alias; retain the existing `upsampled_count() as count` output for an unaliased count, including currently supported case and outer-whitespace variants.
Leave unrelated columns and aggregates unchanged; do not rewrite expressions merely because they contain the text `count`.
Continue returning a list in input order with one output per input column, including an empty list for empty input, without mutating the input.
items.notes: The provided code does not establish which extra parentheses or alias spellings the endpoint accepts; require normalization only for syntax actually supported by its query language. A parser is not mandatory: a suitably constrained matcher is also valid. Rewriting counts nested in arbitrary equations or other aggregates is outside the demonstrated standalone-count defect.

items.defectStatement: The added organization/BROKER_PUBLIC condition in LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() changes a shared predicate from the enabled/not-link-only/not-hidden checks to also reject non-public organization providers. For the reported IdentityProviderBean caller, this removes otherwise eligible already-linked providers from the federated-provider list merely because BROKER_PUBLIC is absent or not true.
obligations: Make getLoginPredicate() accept otherwise eligible organization-linked providers regardless of BROKER_PUBLIC, including absent and false values.
Preserve rejection of null providers without dereferencing them.
Preserve the existing LoginFilter checks: disabled, link-only, or hidden-on-login providers must still be rejected, for both realm-level and organization-linked providers.
Preserve the public method signature so existing callers continue to compile.
items.notes: Only the shared predicate's lines are editable here; removing the extra organization condition is a sufficient local correction. Separating cache-specific eligibility into another predicate and updating its callers would require broader changes and should not be required for this replacement. The IdentityProviderBean usage and cache motivation are reported by the finding, not independently shown in the supplied window.

items.defectStatement: The removal listener is gated by ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, but its management() calls select MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. This mixes legacy removal cleanup with V2 management APIs, potentially invoking unsupported operations when both features are enabled; V2-only configurations skip this listener's cleanup entirely.
obligations: Do not dispatch legacy setPermissionsEnabled(..., false) cleanup to V2 management implementations that do not support it.
Preserve legacy permission cleanup for role, client, and group removal when the legacy feature is enabled, including both client-role and realm-role realm resolution.

Handle V2 configurations consistently with ownership of the permission artifacts: perform any required V2 cleanup through supported operations, or keep this listener explicitly legacy-only if V2 cleanup is handled elsewhere or is unnecessary.
Continue ignoring unrelated events and avoid permission-management work when neither relevant feature is enabled.
items.notes: Simply widening the feature guard to include V2 does not fix unsupported V2 calls. Explicitly routing legacy cleanup to legacy management is also a valid approach; a new V2 cleanup path is not inherently required. The supplied file establishes the dispatch mismatch, but does not show the V2 implementations or establish that skipped legacy cleanup leaves V2 artifacts behind.

items.defectStatement: In verifySafeHtml(), the independently computed common prefix and suffix can overlap, causing either diagnostic substring's start index to exceed its end index. This throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of recording the illegal-HTML message and continuing verification.
obligations: Construct diagnostics without invalid substring bounds when common prefixes and suffixes overlap, including when either string is empty or one is a prefix or suffix of the other.
Continue recording an illegal-HTML diagnostic identifying the key and file and showing original-versus-sanitized content whenever the enclosing inequality check succeeds.
Preserve meaningful difference reporting: remove only matching, non-overlapping context, or retain additional context rather than losing the differing content.
Preserve existing diagnostic behavior for non-overlapping differences and do not change sanitization, HTML policy selection, or which keys are considered offending.
items.notes: The end index need not be negative; reversed bounds alone cause the exception, and the current suffix bounds keep end indices nonnegative. The 'aaa' versus 'aa' example illustrates the indexing defect but is not demonstrated to arise from this sanitizer. Preventing overlap during matching or safely retaining more context are valid approaches. Independently clamping both slices as suggested can yield two empty excerpts for unequal strings, so merely avoiding the exception is insufficient.

items.defectStatement: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), the fallback for a missing client-specific resource passes the potentially null Clients type resource to findByResource without checking it. When that fallback resource is also missing, the permission check can throw rather than deny access, and any continuation would also dereference the null resource during evaluation.
obligations: When both the client-specific resource and the Clients type resource are absent, return false without passing null to findByResource or evaluating a null resource.
When the fallback resource exists but has no associated policies, continue to return false.
When the fallback resource exists and has policies, preserve permission evaluation against that resource and grant only if the requested scope is granted.
Preserve the existing client-specific resource path and the same-realm and resource-server guards.
items.notes: A separate null guard or a short-circuit condition is valid. The shown code establishes the unchecked null path, but the precise exception behavior inside findByResource depends on its implementation; a later resource.getScopes() dereference is also unsafe if execution continues.

items.defectStatement: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() recognizes default view authorization and global VIEW permission but not global MANAGE permission. Consequently, a caller granted only MANAGE on all clients can pass canManage() while failing the global view check, unlike the client-scope view check that accepts either permission.
obligations: Return true from canView() when the caller is granted MANAGE on the all-clients resource, even without VIEW or default view authorization.
Preserve successful authorization through canViewClientDefault() and global VIEW permission.
Continue denying global view access when none of those authorization paths succeeds; do not promote a permission on an individual client to global view access.
Preserve the existing realm and resource-server restrictions on fine-grained permission evaluation.
items.notes: Adding a global MANAGE check or incorporating canManage() while retaining existing view paths are valid approaches. Replacing the entire result with canManage() would lose view-only access. The shown code establishes the global-view mismatch, but does not show canList(); individual-client viewing can already succeed via canConfigure(client), so not every view operation is necessarily denied.

items.defectStatement: In getSubGroups, the unconditional per-subgroup canView filter removes the global-view authorization short-circuit. Callers with global group-view permission now incur redundant per-group authorization checks for each subgroup traversed during pagination.
obligations: Determine global group-view permission once per request/listing, and bypass per-subgroup visibility checks when that permission is granted.
For callers without global group-view permission, continue checking each candidate subgroup's visibility and exclude unauthorized subgroups before applying pagination.
Preserve the parent group's requireView authorization gate and the existing search, exact-match, ordering, and pagination behavior.
Preserve representation generation, including briefRepresentation handling and subgroup-count population.
items.notes: The prior auth.groups().canView() check is the global permission test, distinct from canView(group). Either a short-circuit predicate or a conditional filtering path is valid. The shown code establishes redundant calls, not the precise cost of V2 internals; traversal can include offset entries and, for filtered callers, rejected entries, so checks are not necessarily limited to the returned page size.

items.defectStatement: The legacy Update call in DualWriterMode3.Update passes the original objInfo rather than the result successfully written to unified storage. Legacy storage can therefore recompute a patch against its own stale object, yielding a different update or failing after the unified update has succeeded.
obligations: Supply legacy Update with updated-object information that returns the successful unified-storage result res rather than recomputing the update against the legacy old object.
Preserve the original objInfo's precondition behavior when supplying the replacement updated-object information.
Preserve the legacy call's context, name, validation callbacks, forceAllowCreate, and options, and retain its error for the existing metrics recording.
Keep legacy replication asynchronous and best-effort, without changing the unified-storage result returned to the caller or invoking legacy Update after a unified-storage failure.
items.notes: The existing updateWrapper with upstream set to objInfo and updated set to res is the intended reusable mechanism; behaviorally equivalent alternatives are valid. The cited change need not address unrelated metrics or context issues.

items.defectStatement: The actions at line 47 supply only a Prometheus rule. With the reported ruler-rule guard in AlertRuleMenu, this leaves eligible Grafana rules without a Pause/Resume control even when their pause ability allows it.
obligations: Provide a usable Pause action for eligible unpaused Grafana rules and a Resume action for eligible paused Grafana rules.
Ensure the action targets the actual Grafana rule and has access to the valid data needed to perform the pause-state change.
Preserve permission and eligibility checks rather than exposing pause-state changes for disallowed rules.
Preserve the existing compact rule actions, other menu functionality, and correct rule/group identity.
items.notes: The menu guard and pause component are not shown, so that downstream behavior is a premise of the finding, not independently verified here. Only line 47 is replaceable; the suggested changes to downstream components are outside that scope. Do not treat a Prometheus DTO cast or relabeled as a ruler DTO as valid ruler data.

items.defectStatement: DualWriterMode3.Delete returns immediately for every Storage.Delete error, including NotFound, so it never schedules Legacy.Delete when the object is absent from Storage. This regresses the previous NotFound-tolerant behavior and leaves objects that exist only in legacy storage undeleted.
obligations: When Storage.Delete returns a Kubernetes NotFound error, continue to the existing asynchronous Legacy.Delete attempt with the same name, validation callback, and options.
For other Storage.Delete errors, preserve the early return of the storage result, async flag, and error without attempting Legacy.Delete.
Preserve legacy deletion after a successful Storage.Delete and retain the existing asynchronous, timeout-bounded behavior.
Preserve the Storage.Delete result, async flag, and error returned to the caller, including the NotFound error; legacy results must not replace them.
items.notes: NotFound tolerance concerns continuing legacy cleanup, not converting the caller's NotFound response to success. The old code also returned the storage NotFound error. The cited replacement cannot rely on the removed apierrors import without making its NotFound check compile within the allowed edit scope. Unrelated metric-label issues are outside this finding.

items.defectStatement: The silence drawer is gated solely on `rule` being a Grafana ruler alerting rule, although this component now supports callers that supply only `promRule`. For a Grafana alerting rule in that list-view path, selecting Silence sets the open state but never renders the drawer.
obligations: Selecting Silence for a Grafana alerting `promRule` must open a usable silence drawer even when `rule` is undefined.
Supply valid rule data through the drawer's supported interface so the silence targets the selected rule; do not merely remove the guard and pass an undefined ruler rule.
Preserve silence support for existing callers supplying a Grafana ruler alerting rule, and keep the drawer closed until requested and dismissible through its close callback.
Do not enable the Grafana alert-rule silence drawer for recording rules or non-Grafana rules, and preserve the menu's delete and duplicate behavior.
items.notes: The defect concerns promRule-only callers, not every list-view invocation unconditionally. A correct fix may use either supported drawer data path; widening the render condition alone is insufficient. Only the cited lines are replaceable, so do not require changes to the drawer implementation or unrelated component logic.

items.defectStatement: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronizing with BuildIndex's cache writes, allowing a data race and potentially a fatal concurrent map iteration/write error during collection. The race is real, but the previous BuildIndex-wide lock did not prevent it either because TotalDocs did not acquire that lock.
obligations: Synchronize all access to b.cache in TotalDocs with writers using cacheMu, including the entire map traversal or a complete snapshot taken under the lock.
Preserve TotalDocs behavior: sum successful DocCount results, skip entries whose DocCount returns an error, and return zero for an empty cache.
Preserve synchronized publication of idx in BuildIndex and its successful return, and release any acquired locks on every exit path.
items.notes: Holding cacheMu.RLock throughout traversal is valid; copying index references under the lock and counting afterward is also valid. Merely extending BuildIndex's lock does not fix an unlocked reader. No requirement to serialize index construction or provide an atomic snapshot of document counts.

items.defectStatement: TagDevice propagates a tagDeviceUI failure, but tagDeviceUI has already cached the device before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds. A subsequent request using the same cache key can therefore return nil without retrying the failed write, bypassing device-limit rejection until the entry expires.
obligations: After a failed CreateOrUpdateDevice call, subsequent requests for the same cache key must not succeed solely because that failed attempt populated the cache.
Continue returning the tagging error to the caller, including device-limit errors, rather than suppressing authentication rejection.
Preserve successful tagging and the cache-based suppression of redundant writes for successfully recorded devices.
Preserve the existing no-op behavior for requests without a device ID or with an unparseable remote address.
items.notes: Only lines 144–148 may be replaced, so error-path cache invalidation here is a valid alternative to moving cache insertion in tagDeviceUI. Invalidation must target the actual key used by tagDeviceUI, not assume it is the device ID. The shown code establishes the stale-success cache problem; authentication handling is not shown, and the 29-minute duration is the configured default TTL rather than a guaranteed exact bypass interval.

items.defectStatement: The refresh path assigns the parse-result wrapper returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse to key and persists it as credential.key, rather than persisting the validated Google credential object. This nests the token fields under data, so a subsequent GoogleCalendarService instantiation fails when googleCredentialSchema.parse expects those fields at the top level.
obligations: Persist the schema-validated Google credential object directly as credential.key, without a success/data or error wrapper.
Preserve the refreshed access_token and expiry_date along with existing required credential fields, including refresh_token.
Do not persist a failed parse result or an undefined key when credential validation fails.
Keep the update targeted to credential.id and preserve the surrounding authentication and error-handling behavior.
items.notes: Extracting successful parsed data or using googleCredentialSchema.parse directly are valid approaches; failure handling must remain safe. The helper implementation is not shown, so unconditionally accessing .data is only valid if its return contract guarantees success or throws on failure. The corruption breaks subsequent loads, but 'permanently' overstates it: credential repair or reauthorization can recover it.

items.defectStatement: In the backup-code branch at lines 131–157, a non-empty totpCode causes the earlier password verification to be skipped, but the backupCode takes precedence and prevents TOTP verification as well. For a two-factor-enabled account, an email and valid backup code can therefore authenticate without the account password by including a dummy totpCode.
obligations: Prevent a request containing both a non-empty totpCode and backupCode from authenticating through backup-code validation without successful password verification; rejecting such requests is also valid.
Reject the bypass attempt before consuming or persisting changes to the backup code.
Preserve ordinary backup-code login with a correct password, including hyphen normalization, rejection of invalid or missing backup codes, encryption-key checks, and consumption of the matched code.
Preserve the existing TOTP-only verification flow and behavior for requests without a backup code.
items.notes: Only lines 131–157 are replaceable, so the fix must not depend on editing the earlier password guard. Either a mixed-input rejection or password verification within the affected path is valid. Merely ignoring totpCode in the backup branch does not undo the earlier skipped password check. Broader changes to the pre-existing TOTP/password authentication design are outside this finding.

items.defectStatement: In testCacheIDPForLogin, both cleanup registrations target the literal alias "alias" rather than the providers created as "idp-alias-0" through "idp-alias-20". Consequently, teardown does not remove those providers and can fail when deleting a nonexistent provider, leaving test state behind.
obligations: Register deferred cleanup for each loop-created provider using that iteration's actual alias, not the literal "alias".
Register deferred cleanup for the additional provider using its actual alias, "idp-alias-20".
Preserve provider creation, organization associations, login-availability settings, and cache assertions; removal must remain deferred until cleanup.
items.notes: The admin client's get(alias) returns a resource proxy, so a nonexistent alias normally causes an HTTP not-found error on remove(), not a NullPointerException. Explicit alias expressions or safely captured aliases/resources are valid. The test explicitly deletes idp-alias-1 later; do not require this localized fix to change the cleanup framework's existing handling of already-deleted resources.

items.defectStatement: Line 13 interpolates the unescaped URL into both a single-quoted href attribute and HTML link text in the imported-from footer. URL characters can therefore become attributes or markup in content stored and rendered as raw HTML, rather than remaining URL data.
obligations: Ensure URL data cannot escape the footer link's href attribute or create markup through its visible text, including URLs containing quotes, angle brackets, and ampersands.
Preserve the localized imported-from footer and a functional link whose parsed href and displayed text represent the original URL, without double escaping.
Keep the original URL unchanged for subsequent embed lookup, persistence, and relative-URL resolution; limit HTML encoding to footer construction.
Continue appending the footer to the supplied contents without escaping or otherwise altering the existing article HTML.
items.notes: Context-appropriate HTML escaping or safe DOM construction are both valid. Escaping must cover apostrophes if the attribute remains single-quoted. The shown method checks an HTTP(S) prefix, not a host allowlist; request provenance and host validation are not established by this excerpt. The exact exploit example may also encounter URI parsing restrictions downstream, but those restrictions are not HTML escaping.
